skill.title: Sketch the inverse from a graph
needs: Find the inverse of a bijective function

lines.text: The graph of $k^{-1}$ is the reflection of the graph of $k$ in the line $y = x$. Swap the coordinates of points on $k$.
$(1, 1)$, $(0, 0)$ and $(-1, -1)$ lie on $y = x$, so they stay fixed.
Draw a smooth curve through $(-1,-1)$, $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$ that is steep at the origin.

steps.title: (i) Find the slope of each segment

lines.text: $g'(x)$ is the slope of the graph. Find the slope of each line segment.
Only the second segment has slope greater than $2$, so $g'(x) > 2$ for $3 < x \le 4$.
Go up from $x = 3$ to the graph at $(3, 1)$ (blue dashed line on the diagram). So $g(3) = 1$.
Now find $g(1)$. Go across from $(3, 1)$ to the line $y = x$ at $(1, 1)$. Go straight down to the graph at $(1, \frac{1}{3})$, then across to the $y$-axis.
The first segment passes through $(0,0)$ with slope $\frac{1}{3}$, so it has equation $y = \frac{1}{3}x$.

steps.title: (iii) Swap the $x$ and $y$ coordinates of key points

lines.text: Reflecting in $y = x$ swaps each point $(x, y)$ to $(y, x)$.
Join $(0,0)$ to $(1,3)$, then $(1,3)$ to $(4,4)$, with straight lines.
Label the new graph $y = g^{-1}(x)$ (blue in the diagram).
